sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Most Rails interviews focus on Active Record, but senior roles at data-intensive companies or non-Rails Ruby services often probe Sequel — the explicit, composable Ruby ORM that predates Active Record in some respects and outperforms it in others. This page covers the Sequel Model API, the Dataset API for composable queries without a model, Sequel plugins, and the trade-offs: Active Record is conventions-heavy and integrates seamlessly with Rails; Sequel is more explicit, supports more database features, and handles complex multi-database setups better. The raw SQL section covers find_by_sql, sanitize_sql_array for safe interpolation, execute for DDL, and when skipping the ORM entirely is the right call.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: sequel-basics, raw-sql-patterns, ar-vs-sequel. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
